battle.title: Window Washers: Slide to Win
battle.description: Fixed windows, growing windows and the cost of sliding them.

questions.text: What is the main idea that makes a fixed-size sliding window fast?
options: Reuse the previous window's result by adding the entering element and removing the leaving one
Using recursion to split the array in half
Storing every possible window in a hash map
questions.answer: Reuse the previous window's result by adding the entering element and removing the leaving one
questions.explanation: Neighbouring windows overlap almost completely, so updating the result in O(1) per step turns O(n*k) into O(n). Sorting would destroy the order that defines a window.
The window sums are 8, 7, 9, 6 and finally 3+2+9 = 14, so best ends as 14. Reusing sum by adding the new element and subtracting the one that left gives each of them in O(1).

questions.text: You need the length of the longest substring of a string that contains no repeated character. Which approach is best?
options: Check every substring with a set, O(n^3)
Sort the characters and count the distinct ones
Expand a window to the right and shrink it from the left whenever a repeat appears
Split the string at every repeated character and take the shortest piece
questions.answer: Expand a window to the right and shrink it from the left whenever a repeat appears
questions.explanation: A variable-size window keeps a repeat-free segment and only moves forward, giving O(n). Brute force works but is far too slow, and sorting loses the contiguity the question depends on.

With all-positive numbers the window grows until its sum exceeds 8, then shrinks from the left. The longest window with sum at most 8 is 1 2 1 3 with sum 7, length 4; 5 would need sum 8 plus another element.

questions.text: A variable-size window algorithm has a while loop nested inside its for loop. Why can it still run in O(n)?
options: The inner loop always runs at most twice
Each element enters the window once and leaves at most once, so total pointer moves are at most 2n
Nested loops are always linear when the array is sorted
The inner loop runs only when the array has duplicates
questions.answer: Each element enters the window once and leaves at most once, so total pointer moves are at most 2n
questions.explanation: Both pointers only move forward, so the combined work of the loops is bounded by about 2n, not n squared. Counting loops nested is not the same as multiplying their counts when the inner pointer never resets.

coding.title: Longest Unique Substring
coding.description: Given a string of lowercase letters, find the length of the longest contiguous substring in which no character appears twice. Print that length.
coding.inputDescription: A single line containing the string.
coding.outputDescription: A single integer: the length of the longest substring without repeated characters.

debug.title: The Window That Forgot Wrong
debug.description: The program finds the maximum sum of any k consecutive numbers using a sliding window. It gives wrong answers when the array is longer than k. Input: line 1 'n k', line 2 the n integers. Output: the maximum window sum.
hints: Try n=5, k=2 with 1 2 3 4 5. The answer should be 9 (4+5). Trace the sum after the first slide.
Look at the line that updates sum when the window moves. Which element should leave the window when index i enters?
When the window covers i-k+1..i, the element that just left is the one at index i-k, not i-k+1.
Subtract a[i - k] instead of a[i - k + 1] so exactly the element that left the window is removed.
